content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Reconstruction-error autoencoders can be trained on unlabelled high-frequency telemetry streams to produce anomaly scores without requiring labelled attack examples.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01921","field":"abstract","quote":"Reconstruction-error autoencoders have been applied to anomaly detection in images and network traffic"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-01921","field":"abstract","quote":"trains a shallow denoising autoencoder on 2.1 million unlabelled sessions"}]},{"text":"Semi-supervised learning can improve anomaly detection performance when only a small fraction of examples are labelled, even when that labelled set represents confirmed anomalies rather than normal baseline data.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01921","field":"abstract","quote":"The semi-supervised variant outperforms the fully unsupervised baseline by 9 percentage points"},{"id":"R0856","field":"keywords","quote":"semi-supervised learning"}]},{"text":"Telemetry-based anomaly detection methods address handling of irregular sampling rates, session length variance, and sensitivity to concept drift in streaming data environments.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01921","field":"abstract","quote":"variable-length behavioural telemetry streams in games raises specific challenges including irregular sampling rates"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-09226","field":"abstract","quote":"For each method family, key assumptions, scalability properties, and sensitivity to concept drift are discussed"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's published work on reconstruction-error autoencoders for unsupervised and semi-supervised anomaly detection in high-frequency telemetry streams [SYN-PUB-01921] directly addresses the core challenge of detecting anomalies without labelled attack data, and the broader survey [SYN-PUB-09226] covers practical deployment considerations and taxonomy of anomaly types relevant to event log monitoring."}
